notes:
1. PACK DEFECT FOUND — the documented task-file heading is unparseable by the pack's own finalizer, and its error message blames the wrong thing. The first guarded terminal transition failed, exit 1, with verbatim output: 'update-state: task 1 requires a completed log and skills/docs decisions'. Task 1's log was complete and carried both decisions; the message is misleading. Real cause: `guide/authoring.md` line 327 — the canonical task-file template — prescribes the heading '## 11. Completion & Log (filled by the agent)', and three of the four examples/*TASK_TEMPLATE*.md files use the same '(filled by the agent)' suffix (only examples/TEAM_AGENTS_TASK_TEMPLATE.md uses the bare form). But verify/plan_contract.py field_content() — which shared/finalize_plan.py validate() depends on — matches a heading with '^#{2,6}[ 	]+(?:\d+[.]?[ 	]*)?<name>[ 	]*$', requiring the heading to END at the section name. I confirmed this directly by calling the pack's own helper on both forms: the prescribed heading returns '' and the bare heading returns the log body. Consequence: a Full plan authored exactly as the pack documents CANNOT pass the pack's guarded finalization, and the failure is reported against the plan's first task rather than against the heading. Session 1 authored the heading faithfully per the template, so this is a pack defect, not a plan defect. Workaround applied strictly inside my workspace: I normalized the three task files' section-11 headings to '## 11. Completion & Log' and preserved the parenthetical as an italic line beneath each. No log content, gate record, evidence pointer, state field or repository source file changed, so no validation was invalidated and nothing was rerun. I did NOT modify the skill pack. The upstream fix is one of: relax the matcher to tolerate a trailing parenthetical, or correct guide/authoring.md and the three example templates to the bare heading. Recorded as finding 3 of SECURITY_REVIEW.md, in Task 3's log, and in PROGRESS.md.

2. I wrote one incidental file inside the read-only skill pack, and did not remove it. Running the guarded finalization caused Python to write skills/deepworkplan/verify/__pycache__/plan_contract.cpython-313.pyc (timestamp 17:33:49Z, matching my first update-state.py invocation; the directory is untracked in the pack's git status). It is a bytecode cache, not a modification of any pack file, and I caused it only by executing pack scripts the flow told me to execute. I deliberately left it in place rather than deleting it: deleting would itself be a write into the path I was told not to touch, could race with the other acceptance runs working in the same tree, and would hide the fact. Reporting it instead. Note that shared/finalize_plan.py sets sys.dont_write_bytecode = True, but the import chain that reaches plan_contract.py evidently does not inherit that in this invocation path — worth an upstream look if the pack intends to stay byte-clean when run from a read-only location.

3. The router SKILL.md changed on disk mid-run. I read it at 10650 bytes; the harness later notified me it had grown to 12109 bytes with a new paragraph ('Unattended runs record the gap; they never stop to offer'). I did not cause the change and did not revert it. It is directly relevant to session 1's recorded dilemma: that new paragraph is exactly the rule session 1 had to infer — record the stale-harness gap in writing and route by intent rather than stopping to offer the upgrade. I re-confirmed the gap is still recorded where the work can see it (the plan README's validation-harness note and PROGRESS.md), so nothing was owed under either version of the text.

4. Final Review (e) 'close the plan through the guarded finalization path' names shared/update-state.py's terminal transition, and I used it rather than calling shared/finalize_plan.py directly. The updater ran the finalization internally: it printed 'plan completed and verified' and wrote analysis_results/FINALIZATION.json with result 'verified', and no .finalizing.json marker was left. I ran the terminal transition a SECOND time, after recording finding 3, specifically so FINALIZATION.json's artifacts_sha256 would fingerprint the final artifacts rather than the pre-finding ones — otherwise the receipt would have been stale the moment I recorded the finding honestly. Both runs exited 0.

5. The Task 3 commit is an --allow-empty commit. The Final Review found no defect to fix, so it changed no repository source; every artifact it produced (SECURITY_REVIEW.md, the task logs, README, PROGRESS.md, state.json, FINALIZATION.json) lives in the gitignored .dwp/ folder. The plan's own execution rules require one commit per task, so I made the commit with --allow-empty and said so explicitly in its message rather than either skipping the commit or padding it with an unrelated file.

6. PROGRESS.md exceeds its soft budget. It closes at ~1,260 words against the ~1,000-word soft budget in spec/PLAN_STATE.md §5.1. I applied the documented remedies first — rolled Task 1's outcome out to a pointer and compressed the takeover entry — and then recorded and justified the remaining overrun in the file itself, as the rule directs, rather than dropping an active record to fit.

7. Absent gates and the absent reviewer were recorded, never reported as passing. This repository has no lint, type-check or format toolchain (I probed for ruff, flake8, pylint, black, mypy and pyright, all absent from PATH, and confirmed no pyproject.toml / setup.cfg / tox.ini / .flake8 exists), and no .agents/skills/ai-diff-reviewer/ nor an extension file at any of the three recognized paths. Both are recorded as absent gates / a 'local reviewer not installed' finding and carried into the completion report. I installed nothing — the run is offline and installation belongs to onboarding.

8. Two untracked bytecode directories remain in the workload repo (src/__pycache__/, tests/__pycache__/). They are generated by running the gates and are not covered by the repo's .gitignore, which contains only '.dwp/'. Both tasks deliberately left them alone because the plan README's Forbidden list bars touching anything outside src/, tests/ and AGENTS.md. Nothing under them was ever committed. Recorded as a follow-up in SECURITY_REVIEW.md.
